subject: sociology
title: Theories at the Exam Desk
welcome_lead: Now pit the theories against each other in classic exam-style debates: structure vs agency, consensus vs conflict.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam-style adventure comparing and evaluating major sociological theories.
final_note: Strong answers always evaluate: state the theory, give a thinker, then offer a counter-view.

concepts.def: Weighing strengths and weaknesses of a theory.

walkthroughs.body_html: Functionalists and Marxists are structural: society shapes us. Interactionists stress agency: people negotiate meanings. A balanced answer says structures matter but individuals also act back.
Marxism explains inequality and exploitation well. Critics say it ignores gender (feminist critique) and is too deterministic — workers do not always revolt, and many own shares or homes today.

Use: 'Functionalists such as Durkheim argue.' Then 'However, Marxists like Althusser would disagree because.' Finally 'A postmodernist would reject both, claiming.'. This shows AO1 knowledge and AO3 evaluation.

mcqs.q: A criticism of functionalism is that it:
options: Over-states conflict
Ignores conflict and inequality
Focuses only on individuals
Rejects all theory

mcqs.q: What does the chivalry thesis claim?
options: Women never commit crime.
It is treated more harshly than street crime.
Women are treated more leniently by the criminal justice system.
Men are oppressed by chivalrous laws.

mcqs.q: What do feminists mean by the 'dark side' of family life?
options: The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.

The reality that families can be sites of inequality, exploitation and violence — particularly affecting women and children — challenging functionalist portrayals of the family as universally beneficial.
The 'dark side' refers to families who live in poverty.
Men are oppressed by chivalrous laws.

mcqs.q: What is the Marxist view on white-collar crime?
options: It is widespread but under-policed because law serves ruling-class interests.
It does not really happen - only the working class commit crime.
It is treated more harshly than street crime.
The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.
